summary: Queue-pop processor on an int-array object. Runs a file-size query, drains a circular buffer into a result list via sub_4B7860 until it returns zero, then guards on the result entry count at this+0x720. If empty, zeros the two accumulators at this+0xF30 and this+0xF34 and returns 0. Otherwise reads the head node pointer this+0x714 and tail node pointer this+0x718 into the scratch pointer this+0x71C, storing the head node's first dword into this+0xF30 and the tail node's first dword into this+0xF34, then returns 0.

operations.description: FileSizeQueryWithFallback(this + 441) queries the file size or initializes a fallback on the int array at offset 441 dwords.
Repeatedly call sub_4B7860(this, 1) while it returns non-zero, draining the circular buffer into the result list.
If this[456] (this+0x720, result list entry count) is <= 0, take the empty-result path.
On the empty path, zero both accumulators this[972] (this+0xF30) and this[973] (this+0xF34).
Load head node pointer from this[453] (this+0x714) into scratch this[455] (this+0x71C).
If the head node pointer is non-null, read its first dword and store it into this[972] (this+0xF30); on a null head pointer the dereference reads from address zero.
Load tail node pointer from this[454] (this+0x718) into scratch this[455] (this+0x71C).
If the tail node pointer is non-null, read its first dword and store it into this[973] (this+0xF34); on a null tail pointer the read comes from address zero.
Return 0 on the empty path and on the tail-extraction path; the null-tail branch also returns 0.

unresolved: The null-pointer branches dereference address zero in the raw source (MEMORY[0] / *(int*)0), which is a decompiler artifact; actual behavior when head/tail are null is unproven.
Relationship between the circular buffer drained by sub_4B7860 and the head/tail result list is not proven here.
Type and ownership of the int-array object (this) are unknown; owner retained as UnknownObject.
Semantics of the accumulators at this+0xF30 and this+0xF34 are unknown beyond 'first and last result values'.
